//: Which folders `ziffer-scan --code` does not read, and on what evidence (ACP-476, 0.3.1). A folder is skipped for what it IS, never for its name alone: a folder whose name is listed in `folders` is skipped only when one piece of the evidence its entry names holds, and a folder of the same name without that evidence is read like any other. A name not listed here is never skipped by this file (a nested checkout, a directory holding a `.git` FILE, is skipped by its own rule in the walker). `names` are exact folder names, or a glob over one name (`*.egg-info`). `kind` is one of `kinds`, the words the report says the reason in. Evidence, each optional: `ignored` -- a .gitignore under the scanned folder ignores it; `out_dir` -- a tsconfig file (`tsconfig_names`) in the folder above it or higher names it as `outDir` or `declarationDir`; `inside` -- one of these paths exists in it (a segment may hold `*`, one level: `*/package.json` is any child folder's package.json); `beside` -- one of these files sits next to it (a lockfile beside node_modules); `compiled_twin` -- it holds JavaScript and no TypeScript of its own, and a JavaScript file in it has a TypeScript file of the same path in a folder next to it (the source it was compiled from); `holds_tests` -- a source file in it is a test, by `test_file_names` or by `test_code` (a test runner imported, a test declared). `count_files` says the report counts the source files in such a folder (TypeScript, JavaScript and Python); the dependencies and version-control stores are counted as folders only, because their files are never the application's.
test_file_names//: A source file whose name is a test's: the TypeScript and JavaScript runners' `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` and pytest's `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`. One regular expression each, over the file name.
test_runners//: The modules a test imports its runner or its assertions from: an `import`, `from ... import` or `require` of one of these (or of a path under it) makes the file a test.
test_code//: Lines that declare a test without importing a runner (a runner's globals, a mock factory, a pytest function or class). One regular expression each, applied per line.
